text:
maria: Heads up — we're planning to provision ~40 p4d instances across us-east-2 and ap-southeast-1 next week for the benchmark run and upcoming Dedicated pool. We need Elastic IPs and ENI/VPC limit increases. Listing current accounts/regions and requested numbers below. Can infra help with the quota requests or an interim pattern?

maria: Accounts: 111122223333 (prod-shared), 111122223334 (dedicated-us-east-2), 111122223335 (staging-aps1). Regions: us-east-2, ap-southeast-1. Current EIP per-region is 5, need 60 in us-east-2 and 40 in ap-southeast-1 for static control-plane IPs + SSH bastions. ENI quota needs bump (we'll attach multiple ENIs per instance for management + sidecars). Also checking VPC IPv4 address pool — may need larger CIDR or IPv6 enablement.

infra-bot: Thanks @maria — automated checklist: please include exact requested limits (current -> desired), justification (business impact), and expected launch date. Also include architecture diagram or small ASCII network sketch. See: https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/limits-increase/ :white_check_mark:

sam: Quick thought — can we reduce EIP count by putting instances in private subnets + using NAT gateway(s) for outbound egress? For inbound control-plane endpoints we might front with an NLB (Elastic IPs on NLB) or use ALB + resolver endpoint. Might cut the number of EIPs needed. :thinking_face:

raj: FYI ENI behaviour depends on instance family. p4d instances create multiple network interfaces for SR-IOV/ENIs for performance. AWS regional ENI quotas can block mass launches. Also watch ENI attachment limits per AZ and per-account. If we need persistent secondary IPs, you might end up hitting IPv4 address exhaustion in a VPC — enabling IPv6 could reduce EIP requirements.

anna: Copied a short template we've used to open AWS support cases — paste into support console and include the account IDs above. You can tweak the numbers.

anna: ```
Subject: Increase Elastic IP and ENI quotas for bulk GPU provisioning
Account IDs: 111122223333, 111122223334, 111122223335
Regions: us-east-2 (request EIP limit -> 60), ap-southeast-1 (request EIP limit -> 40)
Requested ENI quota: increase regional ENI limit to 5000 (or per-AZ as recommended)
Justification: Scheduled Dedicated/pilot GPU pool onboarding on <date>, requires static IPs for control plane, bastions, and monitored sidecar attachments. Launch date: 2026-03-25. Contact: maria@redwood.example.com
Attachments: small architecture diagram (VPC CIDR, subnets, NAT/NLB plan)
```

maria: Thanks @anna — filing now. I'll include the diagram and the Terraform network snippet. Will also ask AWS about a temporary soft limit increase timeline and whether they can do per-region rapid ramp.

cloud-ops: Recommend two parallel actions: 1) File quota increase with AWS support using Anna's template (owner: maria). 2) Short-term mitigation: avoid assigning public EIPs to every node — use private IP + NLB for control-plane endpoints, and centralize outbound egress through a small fleet of NAT gateways (or egress ENIs) to minimize EIP footprint. If we must have dedicated EIPs, request them in prod-dedicated account first and test.

maria: Filed case 1234567890 this morning. AWS auto-reply asked for network diagram and per-AZ instance counts — I've attached those. Case says "initial response within 24 hours". Will post AWS case link here when I get it.

sam: Nice. If AWS pushes back on EIPs, we can also consider using AWS Global Accelerator or Elastic IPs on NLBs to aggregate static addresses.

raj: Also pinged infra-sre to check quota history for those accounts — will post the current ENI and EIP quotas and usage shortly.

maria: Awesome — I'll coordinate follow-ups and own the case until resolved. Ping me directly if you need the Terraform snippet or the diagram. :thumbsup:
